audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 14, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jonathan's initiative and armor-bearer power dynamics, battlefield sign, ethnic language, textual ark/ephod issue, panic and defections, Saul's food oath, honey, blood-eating, lot procedure, death sentence, popular ransom, war summaries, family names, and anti-oath/child-soldier safeguards.

verses.restored: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to young man carrying his armor, Come, let us cross to Philistine outpost on other side. But he did not tell his father.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.

verses.restored: Saul was staying at edge of Gibeah under pomegranate tree at Migron, and people with him were about six hundred.

familiar.text: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;

verses.restored: Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, priest of YHWH at Shiloh, was carrying ephod. People did not know Jonathan had gone.

familiar.text: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD’s priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

verses.restored: Between passes by which Jonathan sought to cross to Philistine outpost was a tooth of rock on one side and a tooth of rock on other; name of one was Bozez and name of other Seneh.

familiar.text: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines’ garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

verses.restored: One tooth stood north before Michmash, and other south before Geba.

familiar.text: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.

verses.restored: Jonathan said to young man carrying his armor, Come, let us cross to outpost of these uncircumcised. Perhaps YHWH will act for us, for nothing restrains YHWH from saving by many or by few.

familiar.text: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.

verses.restored: His armor-bearer said to him, Do all that is in your heart. Turn yourself; look, I am with you according to your heart.

familiar.text: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.

verses.restored: Jonathan said, Look, we are crossing to men and will reveal ourselves to them.

familiar.text: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.

verses.restored: If they say thus to us, Wait until we reach you, then we will stand in our place and not go up to them.

familiar.text: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.

verses.restored: But if they say thus, Come up to us, then we will go up, for YHWH has given them into our hand. This will be sign for us.

familiar.text: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.

verses.restored: Both revealed themselves to Philistine outpost. Philistines said, Look, Hebrews are coming out of holes where they hid.

familiar.text: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.

verses.restored: Men of outpost answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, Come up to us, and we will make a thing known to you. Jonathan said to armor-bearer, Come up after me, for YHWH has given them into hand of Israel.

familiar.text: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.

verses.restored: Jonathan climbed upon his hands and feet, and armor-bearer after him. They fell before Jonathan, and armor-bearer put them to death after him.

familiar.text: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.

verses.restored: That first striking which Jonathan and armor-bearer struck was about twenty men within about half a furrow of a yoke of land.

familiar.text: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.

verses.restored: Trembling was in camp, field, and all people. Outpost and destroyers also trembled; earth quaked, and it became a trembling of Divine.

familiar.text: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.

verses.restored: Saul's watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin saw, and look, multitude was melting and going here and there.

familiar.text: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.

familiar.text: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.

familiar.text: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.

familiar.text: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.

familiar.text: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.

verses.restored: YHWH saved Israel that day, and battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

verses.restored: Men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul put people under oath, saying, Cursed is man who eats bread before evening and until I have avenged myself on my enemies. So none of people tasted bread.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.

verses.restored: All land entered forest, and there was honey upon ground.

familiar.text: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.

verses.restored: When people entered forest, look, flow of honey; but no one brought hand to mouth, for people feared oath.

familiar.text: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.

verses.restored: Jonathan had not heard when his father made people swear. He extended tip of staff in his hand, dipped it in honeycomb, brought his hand to mouth, and his eyes brightened.

familiar.text: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.

verses.restored: A man from people answered and said, Your father strictly made people swear, saying, Cursed is man who eats bread today. And people were faint.

familiar.text: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.

verses.restored: Jonathan said, My father has troubled land. See, please, that my eyes brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

familiar.text: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

verses.restored: How much more if people had eaten freely today from spoil of enemies they found; for now striking among Philistines has not been great.

familiar.text: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?

verses.restored: They struck Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and people were very faint.

familiar.text: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.

verses.restored: People pounced upon spoil, took sheep, cattle, and calves, slaughtered them upon ground, and people ate with blood.

familiar.text: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.

verses.restored: They told Saul, saying, Look, people are sinning against YHWH by eating with blood. He said, You have acted faithlessly. Roll a great stone to me today.

familiar.text: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.

verses.restored: Saul said, Disperse among people and say to them, Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, slaughter here, and eat; do not sin against YHWH by eating with blood. All people brought near each what was in his hand that night and slaughtered there.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.

verses.restored: Saul built an altar to YHWH; it was first altar he built to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Saul built an altar unto the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built unto the LORD.

familiar.text: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.

familiar.text: For, as the LORD liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.

verses.restored: He said to all Israel, You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on other side. People said to Saul, Do what is good in your eyes.

familiar.text: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.

familiar.text: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.

translation_notes: Jonathan initiates a two-person attack without informing Saul. Courage and tactical creativity coexist with grave risk to himself and his armor-bearer.
The armor-bearer's agreement occurs within military hierarchy; it must not be romanticized as unrestricted consent to lethal danger.
'Uncircumcised' is ancient boundary rhetoric and may not become an ethnic or religious slur.
Jonathan's sign is a battlefield interpretation, not a safe general method for discerning Divine approval.
Earthquake, panic, defections, hidden people rejoining, and intra-Philistine killing complicate any simple heroic account.
Saul's oath centers 'my vengeance' and deprives exhausted troops of food. It is reckless leadership and spiritual coercion.
Jonathan's honey restores him physically. Nourishment is not moral weakness, and denying food does not prove devotion.
The people's later blood-eating follows extreme hunger created by the oath; leaders share responsibility for predictable harm caused by deprivation.
Saul moves quickly from an unknown offense to a death oath against even his son. Public vows do not override life, proportionality, due process, or parental duty.
The people collectively ransom Jonathan and stop the execution. Resisting an abusive command can be faithful communal action.
Verse 36's proposal to leave no man alive is exterminatory battle speech and cannot be a model.
The royal summary normalizes continual warfare and recruitment of strong men; it should be read under chapter 8's conscription warning.
Saul's daughters and wife are named but not reduced to dynasty assets; later narratives require attention to their agency.
safety_note: Reject reckless secret missions, ethnic slurs, food-denial oaths, spiritualized exhaustion, summary execution, child sacrifice by parental vow, exterminatory speech, and leader claims that personal vengeance is national salvation. The people's rescue of Jonathan shows that communities may and should stop a ruler's lethal command.
